title: Glorying in the Lord
speaker: Pastor Tito Lyro

outline.title: The Folly of Self-Measurement
subpoints: False apostles used themselves as the standard of judgment
Self-comparison leads to pride or discouragement
God's standard is His holiness, not human performance

outline.title: The Measure God Assigns
subpoints: God appoints specific spheres of ministry and life
Paul remained within the boundaries God set for him
Ministry is not about claiming credit for others' work

outline.title: The Only Worthy Boast
subpoints: Ambition should be for the expansion of the Gospel
Growth in faith allows for broader mission fields
All fruit and increase belong to God alone

summary:
In this message, Pastor Tito Lyro examines 2 Corinthians 10:12-18, addressing the human tendency to compare oneself with others. The sermon highlights the folly of self-measurement, where individuals create their own standards of success, often leading to either pride or discouragement. By contrasting the false apostles' self-promotion with Paul's humility, the text reveals that the true standard of judgment is God's holiness, not human achievement. The illustration of the baptism of a covenant child underscores that salvation and ministry are grounded in God's promise rather than personal merit.

The second point explores the concept of divine spheres, where God appoints specific boundaries for ministry and life. Paul emphasizes that he did not overextend his authority or claim credit for work done by others, adhering to the principle of not building on another man's foundation. This approach ensures that ministry remains faithful to God's specific calling and avoids the arrogance of self-promotion.

Finally, the sermon concludes by identifying the only worthy boast: glorying in the Lord. Paul’s ambition was not to build his own name but to see the Gospel expanded into new regions as the faith of the Corinthians grew. The message reinforces that all spiritual growth and fruit are the result of God's increase, urging believers to find their identity and pride solely in Christ rather than in their own accomplishments or comparisons with others.
